doc.title: Buster Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

title: Listening to Someday My Prince Will Come and Two Is One live in Perugia
summary: Rowe plays a track with Kenny Barron; they discuss the ending, Art Blakey and Lee Morgan's Two Is One, and the Umbria Jazz Festival date.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well let me play something for you and see if you can recall.
It’s me and Kenny Baron. “Someday My Prince Will Come.”
Right. It’s got a very interesting ending on it. Do you recall? I think you played that note almost the whole piece.
And I believe this is a live thing too, isn’t it? Like we’re not done yet.
Art Blakey used to do that. [sings] Better buy a Bird’s Eye.
Oh. Better buy a Bird’s Eye.
Frozen green peas. Better buy a Bird’s Eye. Yeah. He and Lee Morgan. Lee Morgan and he used to do that. That was “Two in One?”

“Two Is One,” yeah. We did that in Perusia. It was a live date. It was during the Umbria Jazz Festival one year in Perusia, And that’s what goes on for live five or six days. And they tried to emulate some of the popular jazz clubs in New York, like Bradley’s, which we were at, an emulation of Bradley’s. They had one club that was like The Vanguard, they had another one that was like Birdland. But that’s when we did that. Yeah that was a live date.
